sources.title: National Adaptation Plan for the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
sources.organization: Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago, Ministry of Planning and Development
sources.temporal_coverage: Government's first NAP, November 2023; sector risk assessments include next-ten-year likelihood judgments.
sources.methodology: Government-led, multi-year plan with stakeholder input and sector technical-working-group risk assessments.
sources.limitations: Local risk levels are plan-era assessments, not measured outcomes; scenario detail varies by table.

sources.title: Forecasting Trinidad's Evolving Flood Future: A Susceptibility Mapping Approach with Long-Term Rainfall Projections (2010-2100)
sources.organization: ISPRS Annals of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
sources.temporal_coverage: Peer-reviewed 2026 study combines historical rainfall and projected rainfall layers to map Trinidad flood susceptibility at five-year intervals through 2100.
sources.methodology: GIS weighted-overlay susceptibility model combines rainfall, elevation, slope, road and drainage density, and locally derived land cover.
sources.limitations: Model uses 2007 land cover and equal factor weights, downscales coarse rainfall data, and lacks independent validation; susceptibility is not event probability.

sources.title: Commonwealth Caribbean Cities, Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience: Empowering Local Government
sources.organization: Commonwealth Journal of Local Governance, University of Technology Sydney
sources.temporal_coverage: Peer-reviewed article published October 2024; Trinidad case evidence includes 2023 interviews and earlier planning documents.
sources.methodology: Comparative case study uses a 2022 workshop, 2023 interviews, legislation, policy documents and literature.
sources.limitations: Trinidad findings include two participant perspectives, not a representative survey; some context is attributed to earlier literature.

sources.title: Written submission by the Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government to the Joint Select Committee on Land and Physical Infrastructure: Climate Change Inquiry
sources.organization: Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government, Trinidad and Tobago
sources.temporal_coverage: Ministry response submitted March 2023; training counts and implementation descriptions are dated to 2021-2023.
sources.methodology: Ministry's parliamentary written response on climate impacts, municipal disaster management and adaptation.
sources.limitations: Government self-report, not an independent evaluation; stated programme status is dated and was not reverified for 2026.

sources.title: Multi-sectoral Adaptation Measures to Flood Relief in the South Oropouche River Basin Project
sources.organization: Environmental Policy and Planning Division, Government of Trinidad and Tobago
sources.temporal_coverage: Government page describes the project's September 2023 launch, design targets and four-year implementation period.
sources.methodology: Government page reports project launch, targets and partner statements.
sources.limitations: Launch-stage aims and targets are not audited outcomes or final results.

claims.locator: Foreword, printed p. i; Executive Summary, printed pp.1-2
claims.paraphrase: The plan reports that its climate-threatened coastal zone holds 70% of residents and 81% of economic activity.
institutions: Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago
claims.limitations: National coastal-zone shares do not quantify locality-specific losses.

claims.locator: Section 4.4.3 and Table 9, printed pp.44-45; localized precipitation and intense-precipitation rows
claims.paraphrase: The water-risk assessment lists conflict over water allocation and access as a potential impact of precipitation variation and intense rain, naming Caroni River Basin and southwest Tobago as vulnerable to related contamination risk.
claims.scenario: The assessment gives a next-ten-year risk window; no emissions pathway is stated.
claims.limitations: This is a plan-listed potential resource-allocation conflict, not evidence of a recorded violent event; ratings are qualitative.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The NAP identifies potential conflict over water allocation and access from precipitation variation and intense rainfall.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Table 9, printed pp.44-45, rows on localized precipitation and intense precipitation

claims.paraphrase: The health-risk assessment names Tunapuna-Piarco, Penal-Debe, Port of Spain and Tobago among localities especially vulnerable to flash-flood health impacts.
claims.scenario: The assessment gives a next-ten-year risk window; no emissions pathway is stated.
claims.limitations: The countrywide risk is not exclusive to these places; named locations are the TWG's especially vulnerable areas.

claims.paraphrase: The same Trinidad communities repeatedly scored high or very high susceptibility across 38 five-year February and November maps.
claims.scenario: Maps span 2010-2100 using CORDEX rainfall; pathway unspecified.
institutions: University of the West Indies, St Augustine
claims.limitations: Susceptibility class is not calibrated flood probability.

claims.locator: Section 2.3, printed p.361, flood susceptibility results
claims.paraphrase: Port of Spain, East-West Corridor, Valencia and low South Oropouche repeatedly rank high or very high.
institutions: University of the West Indies, St Augustine
claims.limitations: No independent validation; the local land-cover layer dates to 2007.

claims.paraphrase: Authors attribute chronic susceptibility to low topography, land-use choices and inadequate drainage; projected rainfall may compound these conditions.
claims.scenario: Projected CORDEX rainfall through 2100; pathway unspecified.
institutions: University of the West Indies, St Augustine
claims.limitations: Factors were equally weighted, not causally estimated.

claims.locator: Abstract and Section 2.4, printed pp.357 and 361-362
claims.paraphrase: Authors recommend targeted drainage redesign, enforceable zoning, resilient building design and community-led flood warnings in flood-prone urban areas.
claims.limitations: Recommendations are proposed measures, not evaluated outcomes.

claims.locator: Trinidad case study, legislative framework and policy findings, printed p.8
claims.paraphrase: Most spatial strategies for 14 Trinidad municipalities lacked climate-adaptation measures; plans were outdated and local planners unassigned.
Trinidad interviewees cited staff climate-risk knowledge gaps and technical/non-technical disconnects weakening collective adaptation work.
claims.limitations: Attributed interview perceptions, not representative staff assessment.

claims.paraphrase: Two interviewees cited local funding limits; one estimated salaries and other recurrent costs at about 80% of local budgets.
claims.limitations: The 80% figure is one interviewee's estimate.

claims.locator: Broader findings on Trinidad local disaster management, printed p.12
claims.paraphrase: All 14 corporations have Disaster Management Units; the article says they liaise with Meteorological Services but rely on ODPM GIS flood maps.
institutions: Office of Disaster Preparedness and Management
claims.limitations: The article does not evaluate response quality by municipality.

claims.paraphrase: Ministry's 2023 response says Disaster Management Units in 14 corporations ran public-awareness, Community Emergency Response Team (CERT), shelter and hydrological-observer training.
geographies: Trinidad and Tobago's fourteen Municipal Corporations
institutions: Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government
claims.limitations: These are programme descriptions in a government submission, not independent coverage or outcome evaluations.

claims.paraphrase: Ministry reported 3,000 CERT volunteers trained by 2021 and 170 hydrological observers trained in 2022.
institutions: Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government
claims.limitations: Counts and training dates are self-reported in the Ministry's 2023 submission; distribution by locality is not given.

claims.locator: Question 14, printed pp.5-6; Community Flood Early Warning System section
claims.paraphrase: The Community Flood Early Warning System (CFEWS) includes hydrological monitoring, a portal, SMS alerts, mapping, interagency coordination and community participation.
institutions: Office of Disaster Preparedness and Management
claims.limitations: The submission describes project components and expected benefits; no independent performance evaluation is provided.

claims.paraphrase: Ministry acknowledged funding, equipment and manpower constraints, and minimal local climate-policy integration in 2023.
institutions: Ministry of Rural Development and Local Government
claims.limitations: This is a Ministry statement about conditions and integration as of 2023, not a 2026 status check.

claims.paraphrase: Government reports a September 2023 launch of a US$10 million project for South Oropouche flood, sea-level and water-deficit resilience.

people whose livelihoods depend on basin ecosystems
institutions: Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean
claims.limitations: Launch-stage aim, not an achieved outcome.

claims.paraphrase: Project targets 9,758 direct beneficiaries and 175 hectares of coastal and wetland ecosystems.
institutions: Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean

claims.paraphrase: Government cites flood vulnerability, population density and economic/cultural activity in selecting the basin; CAF says resident engagement is critical.
affected_groups: residents and workers in the basin
institutions: Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean
claims.limitations: Partner expectation at launch, not measured participation.

search_audit.query: Trinidad and Tobago climate change subnational flood drought water vulnerability Caroni Oropouche Tobago localities National Adaptation Plan official
search_audit.outcome: Read the Government NAP and a 2026 peer-reviewed susceptibility model with named basins, municipalities and urban communities; model, assessment and data-vintage limits are stated in claims.

search_audit.query: Trinidad and Tobago climate change water allocation conflict resource access climate FCV mediator report
search_audit.outcome: The NAP explicitly lists potential conflict over water allocation and access under precipitation risks. This is a projected resource-allocation pathway, not evidence of armed or gang violence.

search_audit.query: Trinidad and Tobago gang violence insecurity blocks climate adaptation flood preparedness service access local government
search_audit.outcome: No inspected primary climate or government source documented gang violence or insecurity preventing adaptation implementation or climate-service access. This is a search gap, not evidence that the pathway is absent.

search_audit.query: Trinidad Tobago community flood early warning local resilience municipalities disaster management CERT government
search_audit.outcome: Read municipal preparedness and CFEWS descriptions, reported volunteer training, local-government interview evidence and the South Oropouche project design; status and outcome claims are dated and qualified.

gaps: No Trinidad and Tobago country baseline was listed in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json.
The NAP's water-allocation conflict is the only explicit climate-FCV mechanism found; it concerns projected resource competition, not observed armed conflict or gang violence.
No inspected primary source documented crime, gangs or insecurity blocking local climate adaptation or service access; the reverse pathway remains an evidence gap.
The 2024 local-government article has qualitative case evidence and two Trinidad participant perspectives; its findings are not a representative municipal survey.
NAP service-access indicators have no underlying year stated in the cited passage; the 2026 model uses 2007 land cover and lacks independent quantitative validation.
The South Oropouche page reports launch-stage targets, not achieved reach or current project status; Ministry preparedness descriptions are self-reported and date to 2023 or earlier.

Full-text access gaps: 2019 government Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment PDF, IDB sea-level-rise study PDF and UNDP community-adaptation page could not be read; indexed excerpts were not used as findings.
